human_text:
This is the "SLHE Game Coding Class" game dev curriculum project. Before doing anything else:
1. Find and read the project's context/rules files (CLAUDE.md, PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, Lesson Production Standards doc, or similar) to learn folder structure and asset naming conventions.
2. Locate Lesson 6's assets folder, using other lessons' asset folders as a naming/structure reference.
3. Search Lesson 6's existing content (handouts, keys, build scripts, GDD) for any already-referenced filename for a "game start/announcement" sound or a "victory/end of game" sound (placeholder assets are sometimes named before the file exists). Use that exact name if found; otherwise pick a name consistent with project conventions.

Then generate two short sound effects in authentic 80s arcade retro space-shooter style, synthesized procedurally via ffmpeg/sox (sine/square/saw waves, simple envelopes, arpeggios — no AI audio service is available, so stay in an achievable chiptune register, not realistic/recorded-style audio):
1. Start-of-game "announcement" — classic arcade attract-mode fanfare/stinger.
2. End-of-game victory — triumphant ascending major-key 8-bit fanfare.

Keep both short (a few seconds), matching whatever audio format convention the project already uses elsewhere (check for existing audio files; default to .wav if none found). Verify with ffprobe that files aren't corrupt and sound like real stingers, not raw tones.

Save both into Lesson 6's assets folder. Update whatever context/status files this project conventionally updates after finishing work. Report back: exact file paths, naming used, and whether they matched an existing placeholder reference.

- **sfx_win.wav** — ascending C-major victory fanfare (two arpeggio runs → held major chord), 1.50s

Both are mono, 16-bit PCM, 44.1kHz — matching the exact format of the project's existing `sfx_*.wav` assets (Lessons 3–4). Verified with `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` (astats/silencedetect): no corruption, no clipping, no dead air.

No existing reference to a start/announcement sound turned up anywhere in the project, so **sfx_start.wav** follows the established `sfx_<name>.wav` convention.

I also updated the two lesson-status docs that had gone stale as a result: `Lesson_06_GDD.docx`'s Audio Plan and `Lesson_06_Prep_Checklist.docx`'s "Self-Contained Lesson Assets" section (both previously said "no new assets this week") — edited via their source build scripts in `Brand_Assets/Build_Scripts/` per the project's own convention (regenerate from script, don't hand-edit), then reconverted to PDF.
